thread:
priya: Follow-up from the CP split RFC. Proposal: Admin-CP (hosted) for tenancy, billing, policy; Data-CP (deployed in customer VPC) for local session routing, auth tokens, and a tiny KV index for prefix caching. Intent: avoid inbound network changes for customers, reduce egress, and satisfy some compliance constraints. Thoughts?

ashwin: sounds promising. we must keep Data-CP stateless wrt model binaries and large artifacts. only metadata + routing pointers. also need clear invariants: what happens if Data-CP loses contact with Admin-CP?

leo: routing options to connect Data-CP to our inference fleet: (a) ephemeral peering/tgw from our side (bad for scale), (b) outbound-tunnel from Data-CP to our regional relays (fits firewalls), (c) PrivateLink per tenant (very costly). leaning to outbound multiplexed relays.

maya: security: customer KMS issue is real. two approaches: give us wrapped keys via customer KMS (we never see plaintext) or issue short-lived certs via an enrollment flow so the keys stay customer-side. must design attestation for operator-run clusters.

priya: proposed enroll flow (outbound-only): 1) operator installs Data-CP operator -> generates keypair + CSR. 2) Data-CP calls Admin-CP /enroll with CSR + tenant proof (bootstrap token, tenant metadata, and optional attestation token). 3) Admin-CP returns signed cert(s), permitted route set, relay endpoints. 4) Data-CP opens mTLS websocket(s) outbound to assigned relays and registers routing prefixes.

ashwin: enroll API sketch (very small):

curl -X POST https://admin.api/enroll \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <onboard-token>" \ 
  -d '{"tenant":"cust-999","csr":"-----BEGIN..." ,"attest":"<aws-mlc-assertion>" }'

ashwin: admin verifies tokens/attestation, then returns cert bundle + signed policy blob with TTL. Data-CP enforces policy until TTL exp or until new signed blob arrives.

leo: operational win: no inbound firewall changes for customers. drawback: need to design relay capacity to multiplex many tenants per connection and route by SNI+cert. will prototype multiplexing 200 tenants/conn.

maya: attestation: include cloud provider instance identity or GKE node identity where possible. for air-gapped customers, operator signs an offline attestation that Admin-CP can consume during onboarding.

sam: this is a hybrid pattern: it reduces egress but doesn't cover customers that want models inside their VPC. call it "Hybrid Control Plane" in RFC. we should provide an explicit comparison matrix vs full private model hosting.

priya: good point. also: fallback behavior when relays unreachable: Data-CP should honor cached signed routes + local allowlist. propose default signed-policy TTL = 1h, cert lifetime 15m with auto-renew by enroll client. immediate revocation requires a revocation push from Admin-CP to relays.

ashwin: KV cache invalidation: support signed tombstone messages for revoked prefixes. Data-CP must apply tombstone when signature verifies. no silent deletes.

leo: cost tradeoffs: PrivateLink is simple for customers that will pay, but for majority outbound tunnel + shared relays wins. need cost model doc.

maya: logs/telemetry: Data-CP MUST support local log-forwarder hook (syslog/HTTP/TLS) so customers can keep audit logs on-prem or forward to SIEM. default should not ship logs to Redwood unless customer opts in.

priya: rollout plan: v1 opt-in beta with small customers; Admin-CP supports v0/v1 enroll flows; provide an "egress-relay-proxy" transitional mode if Data-CP can't open relays (customer opts in to allow our relay to open ephemeral inbound).

security-bot: reminder: include CRL/OCSP-ish path or a push revocation channel. short cert TTL alone isn't sufficient for fast revocation.
